commit_message:
[Flow] Add a pass that generalizes executables differing only in constants

DeduplicateExecutables merges only identical executables. Models with
repeated layers often produce one executable per layer that differs from
the others only in a few constants: the layer's offset into a KV cache held
in one global, or a per-layer quantization scale. These executables cannot
be merged today, although the comment at DeduplicateExecutables suggests
generalizing them.

The new pass `iree-flow-generalize-executables` runs just before
deduplication when `--iree-flow-enable-executable-generalization` is set
(off by default). It groups executables whose dispatch functions are
structurally equal, ignoring the values of:
- index constants,
- f32 constants,
- static offsets of `iree_tensor_ext.dispatch.tensor.load` / `.store`.

In each group, every such value that is not the same across the group
becomes a new dispatch operand. Each call site passes its own value as a
constant, and deduplication then merges the group.

Two restrictions keep the result easy for backends to compile:
- An offset is generalized only when the accessed tensor is a global's
  contents, possibly through dispatches that update it in place. The
  binding then has the same offset at every call site, so the generalized
  operand is the only dynamic part of the address.
- Integer constants of other types stay part of the signature, because
  they often compute values (e.g. index wrap-around and clamping) that a
  backend may need to see as constants.

On an out-of-tree HAL target, Qwen3-0.6B goes from 1132 to 1051
executables. The code that one decode step uses shrinks from 140 to 59
executables, and the outputs stay bitwise identical.
